scope: 仅补充基线已合入的两个历史 PR；不是对关闭 PR 的穷举，也不是本次实施证据。

items.title: fix(cdp): support light-DOM node queries
items.body:
## What changed

Add `DOM.getAttributes`, `DOM.requestNode`, `DOM.requestChildNodes`, and `DOM.getNodeForLocation` for the top-level light DOM. These missing commands prevent CDP clients from resolving nodes and loading child trees.

Track published nodes per session, send ancestor and child paths through `DOM.setChildNodes`, suppress duplicate pushes, and clear tracking on navigation, disable, detach, and target close. Preserve qualified attribute names.

Refs #1291. Live mutation events, detached nodes, frame/shadow traversal, and pointer-events-ignoring hit tests remain unsupported and documented. Reject unpublished inserted nodes instead of returning an unusable frontend ID. Plain light-DOM requests accept `pierce: true`, which chromedp sends by default.

## Validation

```sh
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 cargo nextest run --release --features render -p obscura-cdp -E 'test(dom_node_queries) | test(dom_node_tracking)' --no-fail-fast
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 cargo nextest run --release --features render --no-fail-fast
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 cargo nextest run --release --no-default-features -p obscura-cdp --no-fail-fast
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo build --release -p obscura-cli --bins --features render
```

- Six focused regressions passed. Missing-command, plain-pierce, and unpublished-inserted-node cases were observed failing before their fixes.
- Full workspace: 2,359 passed, five existing skips.
- No-render CDP: 265 passed, three existing skips.
- Release build passed.
- Raw CDP checks passed on both Chromium 153 and the final binary: ancestor events, duplicate suppression, attributes, hit lookup, invalid handles, disable, and navigation invalidation. Full Rod, Ferrum, and chromedp application suites were not run.
- Final obstacle course: 33/33 at companion commit 2d08d9a, using `OBSCURA_BIN=/path/to/obscura python3 obstacle-course/run.py --runs 1 --warmup 0`.

## Rendering

Not applicable to layout, paint, or output algorithms. Hit lookup reuses existing `elementFromPoint` behavior and was checked at 1280 x 720, device scale factor 1. No capture options changed.

## Performance

Seven interleaved fresh-process pairs per control, with no compiler running. Baseline b13604b has the same runtime sources as base main 8b49681. One browser worker, identical fixtures and assertions. Wall time covers process start through the last assertion; CPU and peak RSS cover the browser process.

| Control / median | Baseline | This change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000 runtime queries: wall | 1,313.5 ms | 1,300.1 ms |
| CPU | 1,140 ms | 1,140 ms |
| Peak RSS | 61,052 KiB | 61,632 KiB |
| 20 full DOM dumps: wall | 1,295.8 ms | 1,378.3 ms |
| CPU | 1,220 ms | 1,300 ms |
| Peak RSS | 62,872 KiB | 63,548 KiB |

Both controls build 2,000 rows. Full dumps now also populate frontend-node tracking and measured 6.4% higher median wall time, 6.6% higher CPU, and 1.1% higher peak RSS. Ordinary runtime queries do not scan or track the document. An earlier build's shorter 100-query control measured 8.9% higher median wall time; the longer final control above did not reproduce that difference. These are regression controls, not Chromium speed claims.

No dependencies added.

## Checklist

- [x] The change is focused and does not remove existing behavior without justification.
- [x] Tests cover the failure or feature.
- [x] Existing tests pass, including render and no-render configurations when affected.
- [x] I checked for CPU, latency, and memory regressions.
- [x] Public API or user-facing behavior changes are documented.

items.title: fix(mcp): drive page tasks during function waits
items.body:
## What changed

Drive page tasks between `browser_wait_for_function` polls so pending fetch responses, timers, and task-triggered navigation can complete. Sleep for the remainder of the poll interval when the page is idle, and cap the final interval at the requested timeout. Finish navigation outside the cancelable event-loop wait so a poll boundary cannot discard an in-flight navigation.

Fixes #1296.

## Validation

Three new regressions failed before the repair and pass after it. They cover fetch response callbacks, navigation slower than one poll, and idle polling with a timeout shorter than the poll interval.

```sh
cargo nextest run --release --features render -p obscura-mcp function_wait_ --no-fail-fast
cargo nextest run --release --features render --no-fail-fast
cargo nextest run --release --no-default-features -p obscura-mcp --no-fail-fast
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo build --release -p obscura-cli --bins --features render
OBSCURA_BIN=<release binary> python3 obstacle-course/run.py --runs 1 --warmup 0
```

Release workspace: 2,353 passed, five existing skips. No-render MCP: 48 passed. The reported delayed-fetch sequence also reproduces through actual stdio MCP: main times out after 1,000 ms, while this revision observes the response after four polls.

Obstacle course: 33/33 on pinned revision `2d08d9a8e860e423b47209434a9fba9c75e6eee6`.

## Rendering

Not applicable. No layout, paint, screenshot, screencast, or PDF changes.

## Performance

Compared release binaries with main `bd09cd3`. Nine interleaved pairs per control on a quiet machine without a compiler running. Values are medians from process startup through MCP EOF and cleanup. Both revisions assert the same results. CPU includes child-process user and system time; memory is peak process RSS.

| Control | Wall time, main to PR | CPU time, main to PR | Peak RSS, main to PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 300 already-satisfied waits | 96.0 to 94.9 ms | 99.3 to 100.1 ms | 35.60 to 35.44 MiB |
| Idle false predicate, 300 ms timeout | 360.6 to 343.5 ms | 47.5 to 48.7 ms | 33.43 to 33.10 MiB |

Largest CPU increase is 2.4%, within the documented roughly 10% noise floor. No material regression observed in these controls. The delayed-fetch repair is not counted as a speedup because the baseline cannot complete that workload successfully. No new dependencies or background polling task.

## Checklist

- [x] The change is focused and does not remove existing behavior without justification.
- [x] Tests cover the failure or feature.
- [x] Existing tests pass, including render and no-render configurations when affected.
- [x] I checked for CPU, latency, and memory regressions.
- [x] Public API or user-facing behavior changes are documented.
